clue.text: Mum twice produced potatoes

definitions.note: plural sense: mashed potatoes as a dish

parts.note: mum read one way is MA, a mother
mum read a second way is SH, the call for silence (keep mum)

explanation.surface: A mother cooks potatoes on two separate occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' tells you to use 'Mum' in two different senses rather than repeat one word: MA (mother) and SH (silence, as in keeping mum).
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is the British short name for mashed potatoes, as in bangers and mash.

clue.text: Exchanging letters in Wild West establishment?

parts.note: exchanging goods is trading
letters sent and delivered are the post

explanation.surface: Swapping correspondence at a frontier outpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A store on the American frontier where settlers and Native Americans bartered goods was called by this name.

clue.text: Like a horse, one of five appearing during mid-week

indicators.note: appearing during says one piece shows up in the middle of the other

parts.note: the middle two letters of the word week are E and E
a quin is one of quintuplets, five born at once

explanation.surface: A horse-like quintuplet turns up on a Wednesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-week' tempts you to read Wednesday, but here it points to the middle of the word itself, and 'appearing during' puts the quintuplet inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine is the adjective for horses, from Latin equus.

clue.text: Nymph's very down — that shows depth

parts.note: Echo is the nymph of Greek myth who pined away until only her voice remained
so means very, as in so good
under means down or below

explanation.surface: A nymph feels deeply depressed, which reveals emotional depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like low spirits beside 'very', but it is UNDER; the 's of Nymph's just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonar device measures the depth of water below a ship by timing a reflected sound pulse.

clue.text: A French vault that's dangerous

parts.note: un is the French for a
a vault and a safe are both secure strongrooms for valuables

explanation.surface: A French bank vault turns out to be insecure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangerous is not safe, so unsafe is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Noisily denying what horse may be doing?

indicators.note: noisily asks for a word that is said out loud to sound like another

parts.note: denying is saying nay, so naying

explanation.surface: Loudly refusing, as a horse might.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the high whinnying call a horse makes.

clue.text: Try to avoid getting the bird

definitions.meaning: a waterfowl such as a mallard

explanation.surface: Someone dodges being jeered off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' suggests being booed; here it just links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to dodge something; a duck is also a common waterfowl.

clue.text: Postpone coming from inside ferry-port

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A delay announced from within a harbour terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer something is to put it off until later.

clue.text: French physicist and I will be engaged by French priest

indicators.note: will be engaged by says one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A scientist and the narrator are taken on by a Gallic cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Curie was the French physicist who worked on radioactivity with his wife Marie.

clue.text: A posh church safeguarding one of gold

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh, in British usage

indicators.note: safeguarding says one piece shelters another inside it

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic, a church
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A grand church protecting one of its golden treasures.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class (as in 'U and non-U') is an old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric is the adjective for gold, from Latin aurum; chemists use it for gold compounds.

clue.text: Remarkable name for ship!

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable, able to be marked again in new order, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a notable ship's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta takes its title from a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title ship of the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, itself a name for a vessel.

clue.text: No information on gas in spa

indicators.note: no says the following piece is left out of the gas

parts.note: hydrogen is the lightest gas
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A health resort keeps quiet about its gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; a hydro is a hotel offering water cures.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydro is a hotel or resort providing hydropathic treatment, a kind of spa.

clue.text: Kind of reed that's unusual

indicators.note: unusual says the letters before it come in an odd new order

parts.note: the s is used as a letter here, so all five letters count

explanation.surface: A remark about a rare type of reed plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of reed' looks like a botanical type; 'Kind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind person is tender and sympathetic, the sense of soft-hearted.

clue.text: Recognise current learning

parts.note: AC is alternating current
learning is knowledge acquired by study

explanation.surface: Identifying the latest scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge someone is to recognise or admit them.

clue.text: Trying to locate Russian notes in book

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tome is a large book
roubles are Russian money, in banknotes

explanation.surface: Attempting to find some Russian currency hidden in a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like a verb, attempting; it is the adjective meaning tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying as an adjective means difficult or annoying, a synonym for this word.

clue.text: I had turned up after time — that's swell

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue says the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
late means after the expected time

explanation.surface: Someone arrived late and declared it all marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like arriving; it reverses ID to give DI.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or expand, as pupils do; swell is a verb here.

clue.text: Admiral goes from Scottish peak to East End neighbourhood

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
Bow is a district in London's East End

explanation.surface: A naval officer travels from a Highland summit to a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW is a district of east London, home of the Bow Bells.
explanation.definitionFit: John Benbow was a seventeenth-century English naval officer of that rank.

clue.text: Stand for what's laid on the table

definitions.text: Stand for what's laid on the table

parts.words: Stand for what's laid on the table
parts.note: a holder at breakfast for something a hen laid, not a table setting

explanation.surface: A support for tableware set at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small holder for a boiled egg, which a hen lays.

clue.text: Bad medicine in sale — OK to scrap

indicators.note: to scrap is to fight, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Dodgy drugs on offer, approved for disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to scrap' looks like throwing away; it is scrap as in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake oil is a fake cure-all sold by quacks, so worthless remedy.

clue.text: This bean crushed in liqueur

indicators.note: crushed says the letters are pressed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A bean is ground up into a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong anise-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood.

clue.text: Money that's bound to be owing

definitions.text: Money that's bound to be owing

parts.words: Money that's bound to be owing
parts.note: bound suggests certainty, but read it as bound in a ledger, a sum recorded as due

explanation.surface: Cash that will certainly be outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum recorded in a ledger as owed to a business by a customer.

clue.text: Garment protecting doctor in fight

indicators.note: protecting says one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a coat is a garment
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor wears protective clothing in a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting, armed conflict between forces.

clue.text: Cause excitement in prison and at university

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
up means in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Trouble breaking out in jail and on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up is to provoke or arouse feelings.

clue.text: Jet-propelled weapon?

parts.note: jet suggests aircraft or rockets, but means a squirt of liquid from a toy

explanation.surface: A military weapon powered by a jet engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy gun that fires a jet of water.

clue.text: A ring, one of coral

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell

explanation.surface: A ring that is made of coral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A ring' looks like the definition, since the answer is ring-shaped, but ring is the bell sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or island enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Present some women do want

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gift that some women would like.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give or bestow, present used as a verb.

clue.text: Downs the salts?

definitions.meaning: the chalk downland racecourse in Surrey where the Derby is run
magnesium sulphate crystals used as a laxative or bath salts

explanation.surface: Swallowing the bath crystals.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a Surrey town: its Downs host the Derby horse race and its spring gave Epsom salts.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom names both the Surrey downland racecourse and the magnesium sulphate salts.

clue.text: Sixties teenager at start of eccentric fashion

parts.note: a mod was a stylish 1960s British youth on a scooter

indicators.note: at start of takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A 1960s youngster leads an outlandish style.
explanation.walkthrough: MODS were a 1960s British youth subculture of sharp suits and scooters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a style or fashion, as in the latest mode.

clue.text: Kind of rum outraged Don

indicators.note: rum means strange, so the letters after it are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A drink that angered a university teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink; it means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind person is amiable and easy-going, the sense of good-natured.

clue.text: Get angry and turn barrier over

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

indicators.note: over says the piece is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water

explanation.surface: Losing your temper and overturning a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: To go mad is an idiom for becoming furious.

clue.text: Plodding south followed by beastly noise

indicators.note: followed by puts the next piece after the first

parts.note: to low is the mooing of cattle

explanation.surface: Trudging southwards with an animal bellowing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Plodding means moving at an unhurried, laborious pace.

clue.text: Capital spot for place of worship?

definitions.meaning: capital here is the head, and this is the flat spot at the side of the forehead

explanation.surface: A good location in the city for a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city; it means of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The side of the head and a sacred building share this name.
